newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks seen rising amid positive sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks seen rising amid positive sentiment.

text.p: Shares on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) may continue to rally amid positive sentiment when the market reopens after a public holiday, brokers said.

"The share prices may rise further in anticipation of free and fair by-elections today. Low-priced shares in food and textile sectors are expected to attract small investors," broker Mohammad Shahidullah said.
Bangladesh is holding by-elections on Thursday in 15 constituencies which fell vacant after June elections.
"The market sentiment will remain strong and the trend of high volume trading may continue today," said Redwanul Islam of Dastagir Mohammad Adil & Co.
But a number of over-priced shares like IDLC, Singer Bangladesh, Amam Sea Food Industries and Chittagong Cement Clinker may go down on profit-taking, he said.

Abdul Malek of Rashid & Company said there might be both buying and selling pressure. "Both price and volume may fall unless there is support from institutional investors. The DSE price index closed 13.2 points or 1.03 percent up at 1,291.6 on Tuesday. The market was closed on Wednesday for public holiday.
